---
title: Python SDK
description: Fetch and verify deCDN content from Python with decdn, synchronously or with asyncio, through a public or a loopback decdn gateway.
---

`decdn` is a Python client for Python 3.11 to 3.13. It speaks HTTP to a `decdn gateway`. The gateway pays for every pull and verifies it. The SDK hashes the bytes again with BLAKE3 wherever it holds a whole blob named by its hash. It needs no wallet library. `Client` is synchronous and `AsyncClient` is its `asyncio` twin: both take the same arguments and return the same shapes.

```bash
pip install decdn
# or
uv add decdn
```

The package is on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/decdn/). Python 3.14 is not yet supported, because coincurve ships no 3.14 wheels.

## Which gateway

| Gateway | Where your code runs | Who pays |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public, such as `https://decdn.link` | Anywhere with network access | The operator's pool, within a daily allowance |
| Loopback, `decdn gateway` on `http://127.0.0.1:8484` | The same machine, with the gateway token | The capability registered for the requesting host |

The gateway's HTTP contract is in [appendix-gateway](https://github.com/decdn/decdn/blob/main/adr/appendix-gateway.md). The `decdn` package 0.1 works with any loopback gateway. A public gateway needs decdn v0.3.0 or later, the oldest release whose HTTP contract the SDK supports.

## Fetch from a public gateway

```python
from decdn import Client

with Client("https://decdn.link") as client:
    blob = client.get("decdn:<64 hex>")
    data = blob.read()  # raises HASH_MISMATCH on bad bytes

    page = client.get("decdn:<manifest hash>/docs/index.html")
    text = page.text()
```

A `decdn:<hash>/<path>` URI names one file of a [bundle](https://github.com/decdn/decdn/blob/main/adr/appendix-bundles.md). The SDK reads the bundle manifest once and caches it, checks the manifest's own hash, and hashes the file against the entry the manifest gives.

A byte window of a file that declares its size comes back as `206`:

```python
from decdn import ByteRange, Client

with Client("https://decdn.link") as client:
    part = client.get("decdn:<manifest hash>/model.bin", range=ByteRange(offset=0, length=1 << 20))
    part.content_range  # ContentRange(offset=0, length=1048576, size=...)
```

`ByteRange` takes an `offset` and, optionally, a `length`. The same calls work awaited, and a body can stream instead of being read whole:

```python
import asyncio

from decdn import AsyncClient


async def main():
    async with AsyncClient("https://decdn.link") as client:
        blob = await client.get("decdn:<64 hex>")
        async for chunk in blob.iter_bytes():  # a mismatch raises at the end
            ...


asyncio.run(main())
```

A response is a context manager too. Leaving its block closes the connection if the body was not read.

## Use the local gateway

A loopback gateway pays with a capability that a pool owner issues to one of the gateway's delegate keys ([ADR 003](https://github.com/decdn/decdn/blob/main/adr/003-payments.md)). Mint the delegate, have the pool owner assign it, then register the capability for the host your requests name:

```python
from decdn import Client
from decdn.local import read_loopback_token

with Client(
    "http://127.0.0.1:8484",
    token=read_loopback_token(),  # ~/.decdn/gateway/token
    host="example.com",  # sent as x-decdn-host
) as client:
    delegate = client.loopback.delegate()
    # The pool owner runs: decdn pool assign --pool <id> --signer <delegate.address> ...
    client.loopback.register_capability(capability="dcap1:...", scope="example.com")

    r = client.get("decdn:<64 hex>")
```

Without a capability that covers the host, a request fails with `PAYMENT_REQUIRED`. `client.loopback.capabilities()` lists the capabilities the gateway holds, and `parse_capability` decodes a `dcap1:` token offline.

The SDK does not start the gateway. Run `decdn gateway` yourself, or the `decdn/decdn` Docker image. A `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `::1` URL, or any client given a `token`, is a loopback client, so a public gateway you run locally needs another host name, such as `decdn.localhost`. `read_loopback_token(data_dir=None)` reads the token from the gateway's data directory, `~/.decdn/gateway` by default.

## What the SDK verifies

`get` takes `verify="auto"`, `True` or `False`. The default is `"auto"`, or whatever the client was constructed with. `response.verified` says what happened:

| Request | `response.verified` |
| --- | --- |
| A blob, or a file of a bundle | `True`: the body hashes as it streams. A body that does not hash to its name, or is cut short, raises `HASH_MISMATCH` or `TRUNCATED` instead of ending cleanly |
| A byte range of a bundle file | `"skipped"`: a window hashes to nothing. A blob declares no size, so a range on one fails with `CONFIG`. |
| The bundle itself, `decdn:<hash>/` | `"skipped"`: its index is a page the gateway renders |
| Any request with `verify=False` | `False`: nothing is hashed and no manifest is read |

`verified` being `True` names the check, not its result. A body is consumed once, by `read()`, `text()` or `json()`, or by `iter_bytes()`. Chunks reach you before the last one is hashed, so act on the bytes only once the iteration finishes, or once `read()` returns. A failed check raises the same error again on every later call.

On a public gateway, a site rewrites HTML and CSS as it serves them, so a verified request fetches those files by their own hash. Pass `verify=True` to refuse anything that cannot be verified: such a request fails with `CONFIG`.

## When the gateway does not pay

A public gateway answers `402` when its allowance is spent and `503` when its pool cannot pay. They reach your code as a `DecdnError` with `code` `PAYMENT_REQUIRED` or `POOL_UNFUNDED`, and with `retry_after_secs` and `fallback_uri`, the canonical `decdn:` URI. Fetch that URI with a paying client of your own (`decdn get`), or wait and retry. The SDK retries nothing on its own. `get(uri, retry=True)` waits out one `Retry-After` on a `402`, `429` or `503` that sends one, and tries once more, and `retry=30.0` does so only when the wait is at most 30 seconds.

## Point a namespace

The owner of a namespace on the `PublisherRegistry` points it at a bundle. The public gateway then serves that bundle at `https://<ns>.decdn.link/`:

```python
from decdn import Client, PointerDomain

domain = PointerDomain(chain_id=421614, publisher_registry="0x...")

with Client("https://decdn.link", pointer=domain) as client:
    result = client.pointer.set(
        namespace=42,
        root="decdn:<manifest hash>/",
        signer="0x...",  # a raw secp256k1 key: hex or 32 bytes
    )
    result.url  # https://42.decdn.link/
```

A wallet can sign instead: any object with `sign_typed_data(typed_data) -> str` is a `TypedDataSigner`. An `eth-account` `LocalAccount` returns a `SignedMessage`, so it needs a small adapter:

```python
class AccountSigner:
    def __init__(self, account):
        self.account = account

    def sign_typed_data(self, typed_data):
        return bytes(self.account.sign_typed_data(full_message=typed_data).signature).hex()
```

Then pass `signer=AccountSigner(account)`.

The pointer is an EIP-712 signature over the namespace, the bundle's manifest hash and a sequence number, which defaults to the current Unix second. `pointer_typed_data` gives the typed data to a wallet that signs it. The chain id and registry are the deployment the gateway verifies against. The gateway stores a pointer only when its signer owns the namespace and its sequence number is above the last one from that signer.

The package README has the full API and every error code: [decdn/sdk-python](https://github.com/decdn/sdk-python).
